copies.headline: Adam's Backfield Buried Grant By Itself
copies.body:
The running backs decided this before anyone got to the interesting positions. Kenneth Walker III and Bucky Irving combined for 64.8; Grant's Quinshon Judkins and Devin Singletary combined for 11.4. That's a 53.4-point hole at one spot, which is roughly the final margin, which means every other lineup decision was decoration. Judkins and Singletary both missed by about eight apiece, and Zay Flowers posted 5.3 on a 13.3 projection to make it unanimous.
Grant actually won the flex and the kicker — Christian Watson's 30.1 and Cam Little's 19.1 were real contributions — but Jadarian Price (11.8) and Caleb Douglas (13.0) rotting on the bench tells you he had the pieces to make this respectable and started the wrong half of them. Brock Purdy's 25.3 and the 49ers defense handled the rest.
Adam is 7-2 with the league's best scoring average and a 77-22 all-play. No luck involved, just the gold standard doing gold standard things. Grant drops to 4-5 and two straight losses, still the most unpredictable 4-5 in the league.

copies.headline: Logan's Receivers Bury CJ's Flatlining Offense
copies.body:
The wideouts decided this one. Luther Burden III and Tetairoa McMillan combined for 36.3 by themselves, which is more than CJ's entire receiving corps managed, and Logan took the position by 12.3. Add Joe Burrow's 29.5 against Tyler Shough's 19.7 and the Giants defense outscoring the Saints 14.0 to 4.0, and Logan had a 32-point cushion before you got anywhere near the running backs. CJ actually won the backfield by 6.8 and the kicker by 8.5. Didn't matter. You can't paper over three decisive losses with Ka'imi Fairbairn.
What sank CJ was the stuff that was supposed to be reliable. Jonathan Taylor put up 9.4 on a 19.6 projection and Ollie Gordon II managed 7.4 against 16.4 — a 19-point hole from two guys penciled in as floor. We picked CJ by seven on the strength of exactly those two. Logan had his own misses, Justin Jefferson at 8.8 chief among them, and still won by 23.1.
Both sit 4-5, but Logan's 123.3 per game and 63-36 all-play say he should be better than that. He's been losing well all year. CJ, three straight losses and 107.3, is just losing.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Wideouts Produce One Catchable Week
copies.body:
Christian won this at receiver and it wasn't close. CeeDee Lamb went for 33.5 by himself — nearly three times Kaleb's entire wide receiver output of 11.8 — and the position swung 26.7 points in a game decided by 33.6. That's the whole story. Ladd McConkey put up a clean 0.0 on a 10.8 projection while Tre Tucker sat on Kaleb's bench scoring 9.5, which turns a bad day into an unnecessary one. Jared Goff adding 5.3 against a 19.4 projection just buried the thing deeper.
Christian wasn't sharp either. Jameson Williams missed by nine, Bhayshul Tuten by six and a half, and Jordan Love dropped 36.2 on the bench while Trevor Lawrence managed 13.6. He didn't need any of it. We picked him by 18 and he cleared it by half again.
Kaleb falls to 5-4 with a 34-65 all-play and the league's worst scoring average — that record is a loan, not an asset. Christian's 4-5 remains the cruelest in the league.

copies.headline: Leif Loses To A Kicker, Again
copies.body:
Spencer Shrader beat Joey Lunchbox. That's the game. Noah's kicker outscored Jason Myers by 11.1, which is more than the final margin, and in a matchup where both defenses posted identical 12.0 and the RB rooms finished within 3.2 of each other, the leg was the whole ballgame. Add Drake Maye's +5.4 edge over a weirdly inert Josh Allen — 12.9 from the consensus QB1 is its own small crime — and Noah's 109.4 was enough despite Jaylen Waddle turning 11.4 projected into 3.2.
Leif's real problem was the stuff he chose. Derrick Henry gave him 5.6 while Chris Rodriguez Jr. sat on 11.2, and Stefon Diggs mustered 8.1 with Courtland Sutton's 15.5 rotting on the bench. That's 13 points of lineup error in a 14.1-point loss. We picked Leif by 11, which looks dumber every time you reread the kicker line.
Third straight week under 100 for a 6-3 team riding +1.9 luck wins. Noah, meanwhile, is 3-6 and nobody sane wants to see him in January.

copies.headline: John's Backfield No-Shows, Mitchell Steals One
copies.body:
This was lost in the backfield. John got 12.2 combined from Kyren Williams and D'Andre Swift — Swift managed 3.1 against an 18.6 projection, Kyren 9.1 against 17.0 — and in a game decided by 1.8 points, either one hitting his number ends it early. Mitchell's running backs weren't exactly electric either, with Jahmyr Gibbs falling to 13.4 on a 26.5 projection, but Rachaad White's 6.9 was enough to clear the bar John's guys buried themselves under.
Puka Nacua's 35.0 and Brock Bowers' 22.3 should have been plenty. They weren't, because Malik Washington's 4.1 sat in a lineup spot where DeMario Douglas (15.2) and Makai Lemon (12.1) were both available on the bench. Mitchell had his own version — Travis Kelce's 17.3 watching DJ Moore post 6.6 — but Matthew Golden's 32.4 and a 19.9 kicker week from Dominic Zvada papered over it.
We had John by 19, which ages beautifully. He's 5-4 with the second-best scoring and a 68-31 all-play, which is a long way of saying he's good and cursed. Mitchell is 2-7 and still the human coin flip.

copies.headline: Peter's Quarterback Spot Cost Him The Game
copies.body:
The quarterback gap decided this before anyone's second half started. C.J. Stroud put up 35.4 for Isaac, Malik Willis managed 3.8 for Peter, and that 31.6-point hole was already most of the 44.4-point margin. Justin Herbert sat on Peter's bench for 10.4, which wouldn't have fixed it either, but it's the kind of decision you replay all week.
Peter's problems multiplied from there. Josh Jacobs scored 0.5 against a 16.6 projection, Adonai Mitchell posted a clean zero while Quentin Johnston's 13.3 rotted on the bench, and Tucker Kraft chipped in 1.9. Bijan Robinson's 26.7 and Tee Higgins' 20.2 were real, and completely wasted. Isaac didn't need much — Ja'Marr Chase's 31.5 and Javonte Williams' 22.4 did the rest, and Malik Nabers missing by 7.8 never mattered.
Both sit 5-4 with identical 41-58 all-plays, so neither has earned the standing. We had Isaac by 11; he tripled it. Peter's season high remains Week 4's 163.0, which feels like it happened to someone else.

intro: Mitchell survived John by 1.84, the kind of margin where you go back through the box score and realize a single kneel-down or a late garbage-time catch decided your week. Everywhere else the scoreboard was blunt: Adam hung 170.78 on Grant, Isaac put 138.36 on a Peter team that managed 93.92, and Kaleb's 76.8 was less a lineup than a cry for help. Noah's 14-point win over Leif was the only other result that required any suspense at all.
